title: The candle cover
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The cover is the candle, burned down, wax on a plate. The owner says happy birthday. Wood says how. She says the candle. He says it could be anyone's candle. She says it's on his desk; she's seen the desk in the strip four hundred times. He says three hundred and twelve.

panels.composition: The cover: a candle burned to the plate, wax, a slice of cake, the desk's edge.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover showing a burned-down candle in wax on a plate at a desk's edge, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner. WOOD. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner holding a small booklet and speaking to a young man, black and white, no words

balloons.text: It's on your desk. I've seen that desk four hundred times.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner in a cardigan, dry, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner, setting it in the rack. Wood at the door. The count: the strip's; the desk's; hers. Three counts and they all agree on the desk.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner placing a booklet in a wire rack while a young man waits in the doorway with a small dog, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Three hundred and twelve.' She knows the desk.
